n: This revelation was first given to Jesse Gause, a counselor to Joseph Smith. When he left the Church, Frederick G. Williams was called in his place and his name was put into the text. He is to serve as a high priest and counselor to the Prophet.

f.g: A physician from Ohio; he served in the First Presidency from 1833 to 1837.

n: The keys of the kingdom—the authority to direct the Lord’s work on earth—belong to the Presidency of the High Priesthood, which today we call the First Presidency.
The Lord promises to bless both Joseph and his counselor if the counselor is faithful—in giving counsel, in praying constantly (aloud and silently, in public and alone), and in sharing the gospel.
Faithful service in these ways is the greatest good he can do for others, and it brings glory to the Lord.
A beloved charge for every disciple: help those who are weak, lift up the discouraged, and strengthen those who are ready to give up. The phrase comes from Isaiah’s comfort to tired Israel.

f.g: To come to the aid of; to help in time of need.

f.w: lift up the hands which hang down

n: Enduring faithfully to the end leads to immortality and eternal life in the Father’s house, where Christ has prepared a place for his followers.
The revelation ends with Christ’s title Alpha and Omega—the first and last letters of the Greek alphabet—meaning he is the beginning and the end of all things.

f.g: First and last letters of the Greek alphabet.
